text: What problem were `default` methods added to solve in Java 8?
choices: The JVM could not dispatch an interface call unless some implementation was present at load time.
Interfaces could not be used as generic type parameters without at least one concrete method.
Abstract classes were being deprecated, so interfaces needed to supply constructors.
Adding a method to an existing interface broke every class already implementing it, which had frozen the collection interfaces.
explanation: It is Chapter 21's commitment problem: once callers depend on a type, its method set is effectively fixed, and for `java.util.List` the implementers included code the JDK authors had never seen. A default method has a body, so a class that never mentions it still compiles. That is how `List` gained `sort`, `forEach` and `removeIf` without breaking anything, and it is what made the streams library possible.
